summary: Unexpected fallback to degraded variant during staged graceful rollout despite model pin and prewarm success
description:
Issue summary: Customer reported that during a scheduled staged rollout (graceful promote) of h-gpt-7b-quantized-v2 the tenant traffic unexpectedly diverted to the degraded fallback variant for ~6 minutes despite the tenant being explicitly pinned to the new version and prewarm checks returning healthy.

Impact: Horizon Analytics (dedicated) observed elevated error rates and lower-quality completions for a subset of sessions affecting two production cohorts. Business impact: several active inference pipelines returned degraded outputs, increasing latency and manual retries. Estimated affected requests: ~4.2k during window.

Environment: production (us-west-2), dedicated capacity pool ID: ded-pool-05, orchestrator release tag: v2026.03.10-canary, edge-proxy version: 1.18.2.

Observed behaviour: explicit model pin for tenant T-98765 was present in control plane; the serving runtime reported KV-cache warmed; prewarm probes returned 200/OK. Despite that, routing logs show a switch to fallback variant serving-degraded-1 for requests that previously had pinned affinity. Edge retry traces show a short spike of 503 from a single host at 15:21:12 UTC then a cohort-wide redirect to degraded variant until the orchestrator snapshot reconciliation corrected routing at 15:27:42 UTC.

Expected behaviour: with explicit tenant pin and successful prewarm, traffic should remain pinned to h-gpt-7b-quantized-v2 for the session until explicit unpin or TTL expiry; fallback to degraded variant should only occur if the primary variant is unreachable or healthcheck fails across a quorum of hosts.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Schedule a staged canary promote for a dedicated pool with a small initial weight and tenant pin set for a test tenant.
2) Ensure prewarm completes and servicing runtime reports warmed KVCACHE.
3) Induce a transient single-host 503 from a healthcheck probe (simulated) on one node in the pool around the time of weight increase.
4) Observe routing decisions and edge logs for tenant-bound requests.

Note: We reproduced locally in a staging replica by simulating probe latency + single-host 500s and saw candidate fallback in the orchestrator under certain snapshot-merge timings.
logs_and_traces:
- Edge log excerpt: [2026-03-12T15:21:12.203Z] edge-proxy-23: tenant=T-98765 requestId=64a8... -> upstream=primary-07 status=503 error=connection-reset
- Orchestrator event: [2026-03-12T15:21:13Z] snapshot-apply: merge_id=sn-9215 stage=prewarm_success target=h-gpt-7b-quantized-v2 pinned_tenants=[T-98765]
- Routing decision trace: [2026-03-12T15:21:14Z] route-eval tenant=T-98765 -> chosen_variant="serving-degraded-1" reason="fallback-path-elected"
- Control plane log: [2026-03-12T15:27:42Z] reconcilier: snapshot-consensus achieved, pinned_affinity reconciled for tenants: [T-98765]
- Customer supplied transcript: "responses started returning short generic completions at 15:21:30 UTC"
customer_message: Customer reported in support email: "We pinned our tenant to the new model and saw it warm successfully, but at 15:21 requests started returning low-quality completions and some 5xx accompanied by our monitoring alerts. We need to know why the system ignored the pin and how to prevent recurrence."
comments: Support (Maria): Received customer alert at 15:34 UTC. Opened ticket and escalated to SRE. Assigned Ian for triage.
SRE (Ian): Initial triage shows single host 503 around 15:21; orchestrator snapshot merge log indicates a concurrent snapshot replace. Suspect race between snapshot replace and in-flight pin commit.
Customer (Horizon): We did not change our client-side token or session parameters. We need confirmation that pinned sessions won't divert during canary promotions.

Eng (Priya, Orchestrator): Looked at PR history: PR #1549 modified snapshot apply ordering to reduce wait on prewarm. There is a path where in-flight snapshot replace can update routing epoch before pinned-commit acknowledgement reaches edge caches.

SRE (Ian): Applied a temporary mitigation: increased pin TTL and launched a targeted reconcile job to force reassertion of pin affinity for affected tenants. Customer reporting restored fidelity at 15:28 UTC.
Support (Maria): Notified customer of mitigation and asked if they observed resumed normal behaviour. Customer confirmed outputs normalized at 15:28 and requested root cause analysis.

Eng (Priya): Propose follow-up: add atomicity to snapshot commit that includes pinned-affinity writes, or hold snapshot epoch advancement until pinned-commit ack from edge caches. Filed ENG follow-up task.
SRE (Ian): Will deploy temporary config to delay ephemeral snapshot promotion in the dedicated pool until we have a pin-consensus metric above threshold.
Support (Maria): Will keep ticket open until postmortem and code fix are scheduled and customer accepts resolution plan.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered: (1) pin commit reached control plane but edge cache TTL/stale entries caused edge-to-orchestrator mismatch, (2) orchestrator advanced routing epoch before pin-affinity persisted in snapshot leading to fallback election, (3) single-host health flapping triggered fallback policy that didn't respect explicit pin in certain race windows.

Findings: - Pin entry present in control-plane snapshot at time T+1s after prewarm. - Edge cache entries showed stale variant mapping for tenant until forced reconcile at 15:27:42. - Orchestrator snapshot-merge ordering indicates that snapshot A (contains pin) applied, then snapshot B (promote with weight change) applied quickly; an edge process reading snapshot B without waiting for pinned-affinity commit elected fallback when health of a host in B's target set dipped.

Reproduction summary: reproduced in staging when snapshot B's epoch advanced while an edge node returned 503 for a small window and edge cache had not yet refreshed pinned-affinity mapping.

Relevant artifacts: orchestration logs, edge cache dump (attached link in confluence), and PR 1549 which altered prewarm wait semantics.
resolution_summary:
Mitigation applied: forced reconcile to reassert tenant pin (ran at 15:25 UTC) which restored routing; increased pin TTL and added transient delay to snapshot epoch advancement on dedicated pool ded-pool-05.

Permanent plan: engineering to implement atomic pin-and-snapshot-commit (ENG-4821) so that routing epoch cannot advance to promoted snapshot until pinned-affinity writes are durable across control plane and edge caches. Also add a preflight check that prevents fallback election for explicitly pinned tenants unless a majority of serving hosts return unhealthy.

Customer communication: Horizon Analytics informed of mitigation and permanent plan; provided timeline and asked to be notified of ENG-4821 schedule. They accepted the mitigation but requested a follow-up review of rollout gating thresholds.

Follow-ups: ENG to scope and schedule fix (ENG-4821), SRE to run canary for delayed-epoch config across 3 dedicated pools, Support to update customer after code fix release.
next_steps: ENG: Create design doc for atomic pin-and-snapshot commit and list backward compatibility considerations (owner: Priya).
ENG: Implement and land fix behind feature flag; include unit and integration tests (PR tracker: ENG-4821).
SRE: Run staged canary with delayed-epoch config in ded-pool-05 and two additional pools, observe routing coherence metrics for 48h.
Support: Schedule a follow-up call with Horizon Analytics to review rollout gating and confirm acceptance of fix timeline.
All: Add a monitoring alert that flags divergence between control-plane pin records and edge cache mapping for any tenant for >2m.
